newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Jews count cost of faith.
newsitem.headline: Australian Jews count cost of faith.

text.p: Sydney's 40,000 Jews are counting the cost of being Jewish and some are deciding it's not worth it, according to a report released on Wednesday.

The high price of kosher food, synagogue fees and the pressure to educate children at expensive Jewish day schools all add to the financial burden, the report for the New South Wales state Jewish Board of Deputies found.

"For some the cost of being and remaining Jewish is a turn-off and the inability to keep up at even a relatively modest level has driven them away," said the study by a "task force" of prominent local Jews.
The report into the future of the city's Jewish community, estimated that about 20,000 of Sydney's Jews were "apathetic or indifferent" to being Jewish.
It questioned whether the community could survive with only 20,000 committed members, many of whose children and grandchildren could be expected to drift from the faith.
The report also found that up to 30 percent of Jews were marrying non-Jewish partners, and said "guilt" about not meeting community expectations had turned some Jews away.
It recommended making synagogue services more meaningful and a large-scale education programme to help maintain the number of Jewish faithful.
However, the authors questioned whether communal leaders and organisations would be able to cooperate to implement plans to strengthen and renew the community.

Sydney's Jewish community is predominantly immigrant in character, with only 42 percent born in Australia. Others have come mainly from Europe, South Africa and the former Soviet Union as well as a small number from Israel.

The report examined the different backgrounds of the various immigrant groups and noted that some, for example Jews from Russia, came from communities without a tradition of giving to each other -- Sydney Jewry has in the past depended on the generosity of a small number of wealthy families.
On a more mundane level, it questioned whether Jews were paying too much for approved kosher meat.

"Perhaps, also, something could be done about the cost of kosher food. We have heard anecdotal evidence that the cost is prohibitive and is serious impeding observance in this area," the task force said.
"We fail to understand why the cost of a kosher chicken should be of the order of A$20 (US$15.80), more than twice that of chickens otherwise available in the larger community."
